name: Encrypted altar inscriptions, St Martin's church, Moustier (Frasnes-lez-Anvaing), Belgium
ciphertext_pending: Resolved 25 Sept 2026 (LANE B2 bMOU): transcribed from two of Schmeh's photographs (Moustier-130.jpg altar 1, Moustier-220.jpg altar 2), two blind passes reconciled at 90.5% agreement. See ciphers/moustier-altars/NOTES.md. The source post also carries a published transcription credited to Nick Pelling (ciphermysteries.com, 2 Apr 2013) from a different photo set, noted in NOTES.md as context, not used as a source.
alphabet: 26 distinct signs found: 23 ordinary Latin letters + 3 non-standard lapidary shapes (GAM, TRI, REVC; see NOTES.md)

constraints.genre: altar inscriptions are formulaic: dedication (D.O.M., sanctae Mariae, sancto Martino), donor and date (MDCCC..), invocation (ora pro nobis); a Latin or French crib list is the key resource
constraints.images: two altars, several photographs per Schmeh

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Fetch the two altar images once (Schmeh's post, 2 requests) and transcribe in two passes (Sonnet), reconcile with tools/reconcile_passes.py; count symbols and lines. Cost $3.

2. Crib-driven MASC in Latin then French (tools/homophonic_anneal.py with --fix on dedication cribs; Latin corpus via tools/latin_ngram.py); judge in la/fr. Control: a Latin dedication text of the same length and symbol count. Cost $2, Sonnet.

3. If the symbol count is far above 26: treat as a code or a Masonic/pigpen-family script and compare the symbol shapes with 19th-century Belgian lodge alphabets. Cost $2, strongest model for the shape comparison.
matched_control: Latin dedication text, same N and K

judge.note: switch to a Latin corpus (tools/latin_ngram.py corpus) once built; fr16 is 16th-century French

value: moderate: a public monument, a formulaic genre, few attempts on record (Connart, Pelling)
model: Sonnet, strongest model only for the shape question
status_24_Sept_2026: open; nothing later than Schmeh 2017 and Pelling 2013 found 24 Sept 2026
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
written: 24 Sept 2026 by the survey worker (session_013GkMQP9y84gHGG4pSSwaQj), claude-fable-5-1

cheap_test_done.method: Fetched 3 of Schmeh's altar photos (2 close-shot, 1 discarded as too oblique) from scienceblogs.de; two blind passes (this worker + one Sonnet subagent) over the 2 close-shot images, reconciled with tools/reconcile_passes.py (Needleman-Wunsch alignment). N=158 signs, K=26, 20 lines, 4 tablets.
cheap_test_done.target_result: pass agreement 143/158 aligned columns = 90.5%; ciphertext IC = 0.0499 (pass-A-only IC = 0.0492 at N=157)
cheap_test_done.control_result: IC of matched-N (157-char) random samples: Latin (tools/data/la_repo) min/mean/max = 0.0602/0.0722/0.1034 (20 samples); French (tools/data/fr16) min/mean/max = 0.0650/0.0726/0.0826 (20 samples); random/uniform baseline at K=26 = 0.0385
cheap_test_done.note: Ciphertext IC sits below both language controls and above random -- not itself informative for test 2 either way; not a MASC/homophonic negative, no key attempted. 15 of 158 positions (9.5%) are pass-disagreement M-graded tokens, listed in ciphers/moustier-altars/disagreements.tsv for a future reconciler to settle against the image. Agreement well above the brief's 60% stop threshold, so not a blocker. Test 2 (crib-driven MASC) and test 3 (symbol-shape/lodge comparison) not run this pass, per brief scope.
